nodes.goal: The research-backed additions chosen from the PM-role and agent-context studies: rules that carry their provenance, measurable always-injected context, a stale-command check, and an outcome record that closes the loop from shipped to learned.
nodes.title: Agent context and outcomes

acceptance: Every rule bullet in the managed AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md templates is followed by an HTML comment naming the failure it prevents, where it is enforced, and a reference
The renderer strips those comments, so rendered sections are byte-identical to today's apart from intended text
A test fails when a rule bullet has no provenance comment
nodes.goal: Each rule the toolkit ships can name the failure it prevents, without costing consumers a byte of context.
nodes.title: Every managed AGENTS.md rule carries its provenance in the template

acceptance: validate warns for each occurrence of `specy-road <token>` or `specyrd <token>` in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md outside managed blocks where <token> is command-shaped ([a-z][a-z0-9-]*) and not a registered subcommand. Rule (decidable, documented): code spans, fenced blocks, command-led list items (the product name is the item's first token after the marker, or preceded only by a run verb), run-verb contexts (run, exec, execute, invoke, uvx), a token followed by a flag, path, quoted or id-like argument, or a token followed by the word command/subcommand always warn; the only exclusion is a noun phrase: the product name immediately preceded by a determiner, possessive or preposition (the, a, an, this, that, these, those, other, any, all, every, each, its, our, your, their, own, of, with, in, for, from, about) and the token followed by a plain word or nothing; there is no heading exclusion and no other exclusion; scanning is line-based and best-effort: inline code spans that open and close on one line, and fenced blocks closed only by a line of the same fence character, at least the opening length, with no info string; code spans that span lines are out of scope
Known aliases and deprecated names are listed with their replacement
The check never fails validation and has no false positive on the toolkit's own docs
nodes.goal: A consumer's own AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md never sends agents to a specy-road command that no longer exists.
nodes.title: validate flags specy-road commands that do not exist in the consumer's agent files

acceptance: `validate` (or `specy-road context show`) prints lines and bytes of AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and the managed sections per harness, with the documented limits (Codex 32 KiB project-doc budget, Claude Code 200-line target)

A warning fires when a documented limit is exceeded by a file in the repository; user-level files outside the repository (for example ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md) are listed as a note with their size and never produce a warning or fail --strict, so validate output does not depend on the developer's machine
nodes.goal: A team can see how much context every agent session pays before a harness truncates it.
nodes.title: validate reports always-injected context per harness against documented limits

acceptance: Each rule that the review gate, the tool-call guard or validate already enforces is reduced to one line that names the enforcement
No rule is dropped: a test maps every removed sentence to an enforcement point
The managed section is shorter than before in lines and bytes, and the budget meter confirms it
nodes.goal: The managed AGENTS.md section carries guidance, not restatements of what the toolkit already enforces.
nodes.title: Rules the CLI or hooks enforce shrink to one-line pointers in the managed block

acceptance: docs/context-regressions.yaml holds at most ten destination-shaped cases drawn from past review-round findings, each with app, harnesses, prompt, pass condition read from artifacts, and run count
docs/agentic-sandbox-runbook.md has a step that replays the set on harness or model upgrades and records results
The format is documented and the file validates against a small schema test
nodes.goal: A harness or model upgrade that breaks the managed guidance is caught before adopters hit it.
nodes.title: A replayable context regression set for the sandbox runbook

acceptance: The sandbox runbook includes a three-line structured context-feedback block (missing / wrong / unused, quoting the line or naming the turn) in the executor prompt for its scenarios
A triage rule is documented: act only on items that quote a line or name a turn and that recur or reproduce
The pilot's hit rate is recorded in a design note; shipping the block in the summary template is a separate decision
nodes.goal: The toolkit learns whether agents' reports of missing or wrong context reproduce, before adding a question to every implementation summary.
nodes.title: Pilot the context-feedback question in the sandbox before shipping it

acceptance: Three sandbox apps x three harnesses x three runs with and without the managed section, same task list
Turns, tokens, cost and first-round review outcomes recorded per cell in a design note
The note states what the numbers justify: trim, keep, or test further
nodes.goal: The decision to trim or keep the managed section rests on the toolkit's own numbers.
nodes.title: Measure the managed section on and off across the sandbox apps
